articles.summary: Site will add more than 120 jobs and increase production capacity for commercial and military engine componentsNIEPOLOMICE, Poland, Sept. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, is investing $25 million (PLN 95 million) to expand its manufacturing facility in Niepołomice, Poland, which is dedicated to producing complex tubular assemblies for commercial and military engines. The expanded site is expected to become operational in 2028 creating more than 120 jobs and will help meet growing demand for commercial and military engines.The Niepołomice facility already provides precision components for multiple engine types, including the Pratt & Whitney GTF™ engine powering commercial passenger aircraft, the PW800 powering business jets and the F135 powering all variants of the F-35 Lightning II fighter aircraft.
articles.title: RTX's Pratt & Whitney invests $25 million to expand precision parts manufacturing in Niepołomice, Poland

articles.summary: Singapore, 23 September 2026 - ST Engineering’s Commercial Aerospace business and Collins Aerospace, an RTX business, today announced the signing of three multi-year agreements that build on their longstanding working relationship to enhance component support for airline operators. These agreements mark a new collaboration on component repairs and extend existing arrangements for spare parts procurement and lifecycle repairs. Together, they enable ST Engineering and Collins to integrate original equipment manufacturing (OEM) and maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) expertise, providing airline operators with reliable, fast-turnaround component repairs to meet aircraft dispatch needs. The agreements cover three areas of collaboration: New Boeing 787 component repair support ST Engineering will provide repair services for Collins fan assembly electronics boards used on the 787. The cooperation agreement reduces Line Replaceable Unit (LRU) repair turnaround times and improve efficiency through repair-over-replacement solutions for airlines and operators. Broader OEM spare parts support ST Engineering extended and expanded a multi-platform agreement to procure new Power & Controls spare parts from Collins for its LRU component MRO operations. The broader scope adds more narrowbody aircraft components to ST Engineering’s portfolio for enhanced OEM-standard component repair support. Continued lifecyle repair support for Airbus A320 and Boeing 737 LRUs ST Engineering and Collins extended their collaboration on A320 and 737 family LRU component repairs through Collins’ aftermarket support programme, FlightSense™. “Our longstanding relationship with Collins Aerospace brings together its OEM expertise and ST Engineering’s lifecycle MRO and comprehensive asset management strengths to better support airline operators worldwide,” said Poon Kok Wah, SVP and Head of Component Services at ST Engineering. “The expanded scope of these agreements deepens our collaboration and enhances the value of our Maintenance-By-the-Hour™ programme, in-house component MRO capabilities for the 787, 737 MAX and A320neo and distribution and material services. Together, these capabilities provide customers with broader repair coverage, reliable component support and responsive lifecycle solutions.”
articles.title: ST Engineering and RTX’s Collins Aerospace Deepen Collaboration on Aircraft Component Support

articles.summary: Intelligent suite of solutions will enhance operational efficiency and optimize maintenance schedules SINGAPORE (Sept. 22, 2026) – Collins Aerospace, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has secured two 12-year contracts with Royal Brunei Airlines to provide FlightSense™ and DispatchSM services for its current and future Boeing 787 fleet. These solutions will enhance the airline’s operational efficiency, improve reliability and optimize maintenance schedules across several systems, including avionics, cargo, electrical power, environmental control and lighting. FlightSense and Dispatch provide guaranteed component availability, reduced downtime and cost predictability through a fixed-rate service model. Under the long-term agreement, Collins will provide predictive, reliability-based maintenance to optimize avionics system performance, along with asset and logistics support and access to certified spares and repaired parts. “Our aftermarket solutions continue to deliver meaningful value for 787 operators in the Asia-Pacific region,” said Jen Latka, vice president of Aftermarket, Power & Controls, Collins Aerospace. “With a connected data ecosystem through FlightSense and proactive, globally supported avionics maintenance through Dispatch, Royal Brunei will be positioned for strong fleet performance.” “As we continue to optimize our operations and strengthen our network, maintaining a highly reliable and efficient Boeing 787 fleet remains a key priority for Royal Brunei Airlines,” said Colonel Norsuriati binti Haji Sharbini, Interim Chief Executive Officer of Royal Brunei Airlines. “The FlightSense and Dispatch solutions from Collins Aerospace provide advanced predictive maintenance capabilities, technical expertise and global support that will help maximize fleet availability, enhance operational efficiency and improve cost predictability. This agreement reinforces our commitment to operational excellence, minimizes disruptions and enables us to continue delivering a safe, seamless and dependable travel experience for our guests. FlightSense is a full-lifecycle maintenance support program that provides airlines with maintenance solutions tailored to their operational needs. The program is powered by Collins’ Ascentia® analytics platform, which collects, analyzes and interprets millions of aircraft data points to identify performance trends, recommend maintenance actions and deliver insights that improve fleet operations. About Collins Aerospace Collins Aerospace, an RTX business, provides advanced aerospace and defense solutions across avionics, aircraft interiors, aerostructures and engine components, mission systems, and power and control systems. Our global employees are dedicated to delivering innovative technologies to enhance aircraft performance, passenger comfort, operational safety and reliability. About RTX With more than 180,000 global employees, we push the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defense systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia. For questions or to schedule an interview, please contactcorporatepr@rtx.com. About Royal Brunei Airlines Established in 1974, Royal Brunei Airlines (RB) is the national carrier of Brunei Darussalam. RB operates a fleet of five Boeing 787-8 Dreamliners and seven Airbus A320NEOs. From 2018 to 2020 TripAdvisor recognised RB in the Travellers' Choice Regional Airlines (Asia) for three consecutive years. In 2019, RB received a Five-Star rating from APEX and won Four Stars at the SKYTRAX Awards. RB's commitment to safety and service was reaffirmed in 2021 with a seven-star COVID19 safety rating from AirlineRatings.com. In 2021, RB also won Asia's and the World's Leading Cabin Crew titles from the World Travel Awards (WTA), honours it held through 2022. In 2024, Crescent Rating named RB the Muslim-Friendly Airline of the Year and was named the World's Leading Cabin Crew by WTA for the fifth consecutive year. RB was awarded 2025 APEX Best in Cabin Service & Food and Beverage Award in East Asia and recognised as a 2025 APEX Four-Star Major Airline. As it celebrates 50 years of connecting Brunei to the world, RB continues to deliver exceptional service, grounded in the principles of care, community, and ikhlas – sincerely from the heart. For more information, visit: www.flyRB.com

articles.summary: EAST HARTFORD, Conn., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pratt & Whitney, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has successfully completed the F135 Engine Core Upgrade (ECU) Risk Reduction Design Review (RRDR), a major program milestone that validates the maturity of the ECU design and advances the program toward production. The review evaluated the detailed design elements, propulsion technologies, integration considerations and risk-reduction activities critical to delivering full engine life and providing the additional power and thermal management capacity needed to support advanced sensors, weapons and other Block 4 and beyond capabilities across all three F-35 Lightning II variants. The review further assessed the industrial base's readiness to support future production and retrofit.
articles.title: RTX's Pratt & Whitney completes F135 Engine Core Upgrade Risk Reduction Design Review

articles.summary: System enters full service, expanding Army’s air defence coverage CANBERRA, Australia, (Sept. 16, 2026) – Raytheon Australia, part of RTX’s (NYSE: RTX) Raytheon business, has announced that the NASAMS™ air defence system is combat-ready for the Australian Army. This completes a multi-year project to deliver a modern air defence system to protect Australia’s service members and critical infrastructure. With NASAMS, the Army can quickly detect, track and respond to airborne threats such as aircraft, drones and cruise missiles. The Australian configuration builds on the baseline system with adaptations for local operating environments and mission needs, incorporating Australian-designed radar technology. “With Australian soldiers now trained to operate the system, NASAMS is fully integrated, trained and ready to deliver the protection Australia needs today,” said Ohad Katz, managing director of Raytheon Australia. “Sustained combat success has driven global demand for NASAMS, and RTX is investing to accelerate production of these critical capabilities.” NASAMS is a highly adaptable, combat-proven short-range air defence system. The Australian variant includes CEA radars, Kongsberg’s Fire Distribution Centre, the Raytheon High Mobility Launcher on the Hawkei vehicle, a Raytheon Australia multispectral ground system, and Raytheon’s effector suite, including the AMRAAM®, AMRAAM ER and AIM 9X® missiles. About Raytheon Australia Since its establishment in 1999, Raytheon Australia has been focused on delivering capability and innovative solutions in support of the Australian Defence Force’s mission. Raytheon Australia is committed to working collaboratively with industry partners and Defence to promote national security. Raytheon Australia currently has a team of more than 1,300 people delivering high-tech capability across all domains: Maritime Systems, Defence Support Systems and Multi Domain Effects.
